purpose: Define the read-only interface contract between Runtime and the Discipline Layer before any engine implementation.

source_authority.master_role: Canonical Engineering Summary derived from Runtime
source_authority.handoff_role: Operational Transfer Summary derived from Runtime

discipline_engines.name: Performance Metrics Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes runtime outputs and reports latency, throughput, hot path cost, and regression signals.

discipline_engines.name: Reliability Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes runtime and machine-state outputs and reports freshness, repeatability, missing artifacts, and closure consistency.

discipline_engines.name: Security Boundary Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes runtime/import boundary evidence and reports forbidden imports, write attempts, authority violations, and hot path contamination.

discipline_engines.name: Scalability Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes runtime inventory and machine-state outputs and reports growth pressure, graph size pressure, and data volume risk.

discipline_engines.name: Opportunity Cost Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes planned work metadata and reports whether the work is worth the runtime, complexity, repo, and maintenance cost.

discipline_engines.name: Statistical Decision Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes measurement sets only, never single measurements, and reports statistical decision confidence.

discipline_engines.name: Governance Delta Engine
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes canonical state files and reports divergence between Runtime, Master, Handoff, Boot, tk ai, tk machine, and GitHub.

discipline_engines.name: Immutable Audit Log
discipline_engines.interface_role: Consumes closure artifacts and emits append-only evidence references for audit trail verification.

forbidden_actions: Lab or AI creating trade authority
Heavy mathematics inside hot runtime path
Non-critical feature continuation when Opportunity Cost is negative
